questions.q: Write the three mathematically equivalent standard forms of the displacement equation for SHM, and state the physical meaning of each symbol with its SI unit.
questions.a: The three forms are: (1) x(t) = A cos(ωt + φ), (2) x(t) = A sin(ωt + φ'), (3) x(t) = C cos ωt + D sin ωt. In (1): A = amplitude (m), ω = angular frequency (rad/s), φ = phase constant (rad). In (3): C and D are constants determined by initial conditions (m). A wrong answer (e.g., writing x = A sin ωt only, or omitting φ, or confusing ω with frequency ν) reveals the student has not internalized the generality of the SHM solution and will struggle with initial-condition problems.

questions.q: A block on a frictionless horizontal surface is attached to a spring (k = 200 N/m). The block is pulled 5 cm to the right and released from rest at t = 0. Explain why the displacement equation must be x(t) = A cos(ωt) and not x(t) = A sin(ωt) for this specific initial condition, without solving for A and ω.
questions.a: At t = 0, the block is at maximum positive displacement (x = +A) with zero velocity. The cosine function gives cos(0) = 1 (maximum) and its derivative –ωA sin(0) = 0 (zero velocity), matching both conditions. The sine function gives sin(0) = 0 (zero displacement) and derivative ωA cos(0) = ωA (maximum velocity), which contradicts the given initial conditions. A student who cannot explain this confuses the mathematical forms with the physical initial conditions and will arbitrarily choose sine or cosine, leading to incorrect phase constants.

questions.q: A 0.5 kg mass is attached to a spring of force constant 50 N/m on a horizontal frictionless table. The mass is displaced 10 cm from equilibrium and released from rest. Calculate (a) the angular frequency ω, (b) the time period T, (c) the maximum speed v_max, and (d) the speed when the displacement is 5 cm. Show all steps with unit conversions.
questions.a:
Given: m = 0.5 kg, k = 50 N/m, A = 10 cm = 0.10 m.
Step 1: ω = √(k/m) = √(50/0.5) = √100 = 10 rad/s.
Step 2: T = 2π/ω = 2π/10 = 0.628 s.
Step 3: v_max = ωA = 10 × 0.10 = 1.0 m/s.
Step 4: At x = 5 cm = 0.05 m, v = ω√(A² – x²) = 10 × √(0.10² – 0.05²) = 10 × √(0.01 – 0.0025) = 10 × √0.0075 = 10 × 0.0866 = 0.866 m/s.
A wrong answer (e.g., using A = 10 without converting to m, giving v_max = 100 m/s) reveals a unit-conversion error. A student using v = ωx instead of v = ω√(A² – x²) confuses the velocity-displacement relation.

questions.q: Two identical springs (k = 100 N/m each) are attached to a 2 kg block in two configurations: (i) parallel on both sides (as in NCERT Fig. 13.14), (ii) in series on one side. Compare the time periods of oscillation for the two configurations. Which is larger and by what factor?
questions.a:
For (i) parallel on both sides: each spring exerts –kx, net F = –2kx, so k_eff = 2k = 200 N/m. ω₁ = √(k_eff/m) = √(200/2) = 10 rad/s. T₁ = 2π/10 = 0.628 s.
For (ii) series on one side: 1/k_eff = 1/k + 1/k = 2/k → k_eff = k/2 = 50 N/m. ω₂ = √(50/2) = 5 rad/s. T₂ = 2π/5 = 1.256 s.
T₂/T₁ = 2. The series configuration has twice the period. A student who thinks series gives larger k_eff (adding spring constants) or who uses k_eff = k for series reveals confusion between series/parallel spring combinations — a critical error for spring-network problems.

questions.q: A student solves an SHM problem: "A 1 kg block on a spring (k = 16 N/m) is displaced 8 cm and released. Find the kinetic energy when x = 4 cm." Their working: ω = √(16/1) = 4 rad/s, A = 8 cm, v = ω√(A² – x²) = 4√(8² – 4²) = 4√48 = 27.7 cm/s, KE = ½mv² = 0.5 × 1 × (27.7)² = 384 J. Identify the error and give the correct answer.
questions.a: The student used cm without converting to meters. A = 8 cm = 0.08 m, x = 4 cm = 0.04 m. Correct: v = 4√(0.08² – 0.04²) = 4√(0.0064 – 0.0016) = 4√0.0048 = 4 × 0.0693 = 0.277 m/s. KE = 0.5 × 1 × (0.277)² = 0.0384 J. Alternatively, use energy directly: E_total = ½kA² = 0.5 × 16 × 0.08² = 0.0512 J, PE at x=0.04 = 0.5 × 16 × 0.04² = 0.0128 J, KE = 0.0512 – 0.0128 = 0.0384 J. The student's answer of 384 J is off by a factor of 10⁴ due to cm² vs m². This reveals a pervasive unit-inconsistency habit that invalidates all energy calculations.

questions.q: Design a real-world experiment using only a smartphone, a spring, a known mass, and a ruler to determine the spring constant k. Describe the procedure, the measurements to take, the formula to use, and how to minimize error. Assume the phone can record video at 30 fps.
questions.a: Procedure: (1) Hang the spring vertically, attach the known mass m, let it settle at equilibrium. (2) Pull the mass down ~2 cm, release, and record vertical oscillation video. (3) Use video analysis (frame-by-frame) to track the mass position vs time for 10+ oscillations. (4) Plot y(t), fit to y = A cos(ωt + φ) to extract ω, or measure time for 10 oscillations (10T) and compute T = (10T)/10, then ω = 2π/T. (5) Calculate k = mω². Minimize error: use small amplitude (SHM approximation), measure 10T not 1T, ensure spring mass ≪ m, use a rigid support. A poor answer (e.g., "measure stretch with mass and use mg = kx") uses static method, not dynamic SHM, and ignores the experimental design aspect. This reveals inability to translate theory into a practical measurement protocol.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Word problems in SHM ______ require translating a physical oscillatory system (spring-mass, simple pendulum, floating body, U-tube, etc.) into the standard mathematical model x(t) = A cos(ωt + φ) or its equivalents, identifying parameters (amplitude A, angular frequency ω, phase constant φ) from given conditions, and solving for unknown kinematic or dynamic quantities (displacement, velocity, acceleration, energy, time period) using SHM equations with proper SI units.
Fill in the blank: Observe a car's suspension ______ when it hits a speed breaker — the car oscillates up and down before settling.
Fill in the blank: Third, write the displacement equation using initial conditions (position and velocity at t=______) to find A and φ.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can independently read a word problem, identify the physical system as executing SHM, extract all given parameters with correct units, choose the appropriate equation form (displacement, velocity, acceleration, energy, or time period), set up the mathematical model with correct initial/boundary conditions, solve.
